TWO SAFETY NETS the project's backlog asks for, from real incidents:
1. Node drift. Two months of Node upgrades broke the better-sqlite3 native binding (NODE_MODULE_VERSION mismatch); `npm rebuild better-sqlite3` fixed it, but nothing warned. Add scraper/.nvmrc pinning the major version of the Node that works on this machine today (run `node -v`), and scraper/scripts/preflight.js: a small CommonJS script, also usable as a module (`require('./preflight').preflight()`), that (a) compares process.version's major to .nvmrc and warns clearly if they differ, (b) tries to load better-sqlite3 and open an in-memory database, and on failure prints the exact fix (`cd scraper && npm rebuild better-sqlite3`) and exits non-zero, (c) on success prints one line naming the Node version and that better-sqlite3 loaded. Run as a script it exits 0 when all is well. Add an npm script "preflight" in scraper/package.json.
2. Backups before destructive runs. A cascade delete once wiped relationship tables mid-scrape and recovery was painful. Add scraper/scripts/lib/backup-db.js exporting backupDb(dbPath, { now = new Date(), keep = 10 } = {}): copy the database file to <dir of dbPath>/backups/<basename>.<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMM> (UTC, from `now`), creating the folder if needed, never overwriting an existing backup (add a numeric suffix), pruning to the newest `keep` backups, and returning the new file's absolute path. Call preflight and then backupDb at the START of scraper/scripts/scrape-all.js and scraper/scripts/reparse-characters.js, before either opens the database for writing, printing the backup path; a --no-backup flag skips the copy. Keep those two edits as small as possible and do not change what the scripts otherwise do. Document both in scraper/CLAUDE.md in the style of its existing script list (a few lines, no restructuring).
